meta.title: Risk Band Classification & Action Framework
meta.context: NABARD Hackathon 2026 - AI-Driven Cash Flow Prediction & Risk Flagging System for Rural Micro Enterprises
meta.note: Band thresholds are not specified in the problem statement PDF; they are derived from percentile analysis of final_coldstart_training.csv (24,960 rows, 5 sectors, 3 entity types).
meta.pipeline: Regression model outputs a 6-month forecasted net cash flow series (per-month). This framework consumes that forecast plus current-state features to assign a band and compose actions.

cash_flow_trajectory.description: Primary axis. Derived from the regression model's 6-month forecast series, not a single number, so a temporary dip isn't over-weighted.
cash_flow_trajectory.green: Forecast stays positive across the full horizon; flat or growing trend.
cash_flow_trajectory.amber: Forecast is positive but flat/declining trend, OR dips negative in exactly 1 month of the horizon.
cash_flow_trajectory.red: Forecast is negative in 2 or more months of the horizon, OR cumulative 6-month forecast is negative.

liquidity_buffer.description: Secondary axis. Current-state ability to absorb a shock, independent of the forecast direction.
liquidity_buffer.data_note: Among enterprises with loans, median debt_service_cov in training data is ~0.96 and the 25th percentile is negative, so the 0.75 cutoff sits in a densely populated, meaningful zone.

external_stress_overlay.description: Tertiary axis. Does not set the band alone but attaches explanatory context and can escalate a borderline case. Sector-direction sensitivity applies (see driver_overlays).

combination_rule: overall_band = worst(cash_flow_trajectory, liquidity_buffer). Compounding shock rule: if overall_band would be green but 2 or more external_stress_overlay flags are simultaneously active (e.g. climate stress + market stress, or either stress + new-business overlay), downgrade to amber. External stress and new-business flags always attach their overlay action text regardless of whether they change the band.

climate_stress_deficit.sector_sensitivity: Input-cost sensitive sectors (dairy, poultry, food_processing) are affected via feed/raw material prices; demand-sensitive sectors (rural_retail, handicrafts) are affected via local purchasing power.
